sources.title: CIBR institutional account of first-in-human GA002 chemogenetic neuromodulation
sources.access_scope: Full institutional report; the clinical paper's participant-level tables and protocol were not supplied by this read.
observations: Reports three unilateral hippocampal-sclerosis mesial temporal-lobe epilepsy participants, substantial early seizure reduction and two seizure-free people during eight-to-twelve-month follow-up.
Describes safety as primary, efficacy as secondary, and blinded assessors.
Describes seizure recurrence associated with temporary interruption of activating medication and renewed control after restart.
contradictions_or_reconciliation: Registry blinding=None and institutional blinded-assessor wording require protocol clarification; an open-label intervention can use blinded outcome adjudication.
Institutional longitudinal claims are not independent replication or a controlled withdrawal experiment.
limitations: Investigator-associated institutional account, not the full clinical report.
No complete adverse-event denominator or uncommon-risk estimate.
Stoppable ligand activation does not reverse persistent gene exposure.

sources.title: Collins et al., Encapsulation of AAVs into Protein Vault Nanoparticles as a Novel Solution to Gene Therapy's Neutralizing Antibody Problem
sources.retrieval_method: Firecrawl DOI scrape resolving to full ACS article
sources.access_scope: Full open-access HTML main text, figure legends and discussion. Review focused on model, serum origin, comparator meaning and translational limits.
observations: The neutralization comparison uses cultured CHO-Lec2 cells and serum from immunized mice.
Vault-packaged AAV retains transduction with neutralizing serum; an unpackaged vault/AAV mixture performs poorly in that condition.
Without neutralizing serum, both packaged preparation and unpackaged mixture enhance transduction, so general uptake improvement is not specific proof of shielding.
The authors frame human eligibility and eventual repeat dosing as future possibilities; no human-serum cohort or in-vivo redosing outcome is reported.
sources.retrieval_change: Full-text scope and comparator clarification for an already-known publication.
contradictions_or_reconciliation: Broad immune-invisibility language is not a universal clinical property; the discussion itself notes a vault-autoantibody context.
The principal figure does not provide a clear independent-replicate or serum-donor denominator; none was inferred.
limitations: No patient benefit, repeat-dosing success or human eligibility established.
No current ownership, available license or commercial terms inspected.
Manufacturing and intervention procedures were not reproduced in the decision artifacts.
